title: The investigation of pelvic incidence as a possible risk factor for the development of insufficiency fractures of the pelvic ring - a retrospective multicentre study
summary:
Fragility fractures of the patients are injuries of the eldery patient with a mean age >80 years. Most of the patients are female (75-80%). These fractures occur after low-energy accidents and can even occur spontanously without any trauma in patient`s history. The Pelvic Incidence is a radiological parameter describing the spatial position of the Os sacrum (part of the posterior pelvic ring). Previously published studies showed that the Pelvic Incidence differs substantially in several lumbosacral and pelvic disorders. 
The current multicenter study (a study consisting of several participating hospitals) analyzes retrospectively (the data and images are already colleceted), if the Pelvic Incidence differs in patients with fragility fractures of the pelvis compared to patients of the same age and male/female ratio without a fracture. Each participating clinic contributes 25 patients with a fragility fracture of the pelvis. The fifth clinic contributes 100 patients with comparable age and gender distribution without fragility fractures of the pelvis. After analyzing the Pelvic incidence for both groups an additional analysis will be performed to check whether the Pelvic incidence correlates with the treatment.

interventions.name: 100 Patient*innen mit einer CT-Bildgebung des Beckens ohne Insuffizienzfrakturen

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a diagnosed fragility fracture of the pelvis and a CT.
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete medical records, known concomitant diseases (except osteoporosis), or postoperative conditions that may influence spinopelvic parameters, such as previous spine, hip, or knee surgery; metastases in the spine; or known extremity shortening.
